We show that unless the falsity propositional constant is part of the defeasible assumptions, the grounded semantics lacks most of the desirable properties it has in abstract argumentation frameworks (AAFs), and that for simple definitions of the contrariness operator and the attacks relations, preferred and stable semantics are reduced to naive semantics.
